transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-18
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Carter (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (HelixMed Head Cloud Eng), Dr. Samir Patel (CTO), Maya Lin (Security Architect)
Shared links: Redwood private deployment doc (internal link), security-pack.pdf, pricing_sheet.xlsx, benchmark-spreadsheet.csv

[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. quick intros, i'm aisha carter, account lead for redwood, with diego from our se team. 
[00:12] Lena: hi all, lena here, i'll kick off, we're evaluating private deployment options for our inference workloads, we have PHI concerns and need VPC isolation.
[00:20] Diego: great, thanks lena. real quick, high level, we'll cover network topology options (VPC peering, private endpoints), region constraints, kms/encryption, and an optional Dedicated trial if you want to run benchmarks.
[00:30] Samir: sounds good, our timelines — we want to decide in 6-8 weeks, pilot in september. cost is important but security is gating.
[00:40] Maya: yeah, SOC2 and audit logs are musts. also curious about SSO and RBAC integration.

[02:05] Diego: to understand constraints, can you share current infra? like cloud provider, VPC CIDRs, whether you allow peering to third-party, egress rules, and if you require private endpoints only.
[02:22] Lena: we're on AWS, prod in us-east-1 and us-west-2. VPCs are fairly locked down — no internet egress from prod except through NAT for approved services. we can't accept cross-account peering with unknown tenants; would prefer private endpoint into our VPC or an AWS Transit Gateway arrangement.
[02:45] Aisha: ok got it. Redwood Private supports both models: we can offer Private with VPC peering, or Private with Private Link / interface endpoints. dedicated reserved pools can be brought into your VPC via peering or TGW.

[04:10] Diego: small note, in some notes people call it "redwood privates" or "redwood dedicated" interchangeably; we use Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC) vs Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity we manage). for clarity, which are you leaning to?
[04:28] Samir: prefer customer managed private (private/vpc) for data control, but open to dedicated if the latency/cost trade makes sense. we need to understand IP allocation, ENI counts, and whether we need static IPs for allowlists.

[05:02] Diego: totally. for interface endpoints (PrivateLink) we provide endpoints with stable ENIs and private IPs in your subnets. for peering/TGW models, we'll publish the service CIDRs that need to be routable. note: peering doesn't support transitive routing unless you use TGW.
[05:20] Maya: what's the service CIDR size typically? we've got tight /22s.
[05:27] Diego: typically small, like a /28-/24 depending on scale. for a pilot you'd likely need a few IPs for control plane and then worker ENIs scale with throughput. we'll share a sizing table.

[07:00] Lena: also concerned about egress / nat. our security team won't allow outbound calls to arbitrary endpoints. can redwood support whitelisting of endpoints and restrict calls to region-only?
[07:15] Diego: yes. if you use PrivateLink, traffic stays in your VPC and goes over AWS backbone to Redwood region where service runs; you can restrict egress to specific managed endpoints. if you go peering, routes will send traffic to our subnets — same principle. we also support VPC endpoint policies.

[08:40] Samir: region constraints: we need inference in us-east-1 only for now due to data residency. do you have capacity there for our model sizes (we plan to run MPT-30B and some 70B variants)?
[08:55] Aisha: we maintain capacity across regions; capacity for large models depends on hardware mapping. for heavy models, Dedicated GPU pools with A100/H100 class are typical. with Private you can either have our infra in your region or use cross-region with strict network controls — but for residency, we'll keep it us-east-1.
[09:20] Diego: slight caveat: very large models like 70B could be on different hardware families; performance varies. we recommend a quick perf benchmark on Dedicated to confirm tail latency and throughput.

[11:10] Maya: KMS and key management — our compliance requires CMK control. can we bring our own key and have logs for envelope encryption?
[11:22] Diego: yes, we support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) for private deployments; logs are available and integrated into audit trail. our private control plane can restrict access and we can forward audit logs to your CloudWatch or S3 bucket.

[12:40] Lena: how about SSO, SCIM and role mapping?
[12:47] Aisha: we support SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning in the console. RBAC roles can be mapped to your IdP groups; for Private we also provide tighter role enforcement and option to disable console access for certain roles.

[14:05] Samir: on the network side, what's the expected troubleshooting flow? if a call fails with 503, who is the first responder and how do we collect packet-level info?
[14:20] Diego: our SEs get the first escalation. for Private deployments we provide enhanced tracing hooks and packet flow diagrams; we don't collect raw packet captures by default but we can help you set up VPC Flow Logs and point to relevant ENI IDs. we'll provide a runbook for triage.

[16:00] Lena: there are procurement constraints: we may need a data processing addendum and proof of grants for certain regs. is there a standard DPA and are you open to amendments?
[16:12] Aisha: yes, we have standard DPA and security addenda. for enterprise contracts we can negotiate addendums. i'll include our legal and compliance contact in the follow-up docs.

[18:50] Maya: curious about failover — if us-east goes down, do you have automatic fallback to another region? and what happens to private endpoints?
[19:05] Diego: for Private with peering/TGW, failover requires routing changes or pre-established peering in secondary region. we offer canary routing policies and automated fallback to compatible model variants in another region, but private endpoints are region-scoped, so you'd need to set up endpoints in the backup region too and accept cross-region replication requirements.

[21:40] Samir: ok makes sense. what about data retention and logs? retention windows and how to purge?
[21:52] Aisha: customers can set retention policies; for Private deployments we can set zero retention for request bodies if required and keep only minimal audit metadata. we'll document retention settings and provide API-based purge endpoints.

[24:00] Lena: pricing question — is Dedicated always cheaper per token? sometimes we'd rather use hosted for burst.
[24:10] Aisha: Dedicated provides predictable unit economics for steady throughput; hosted is simplest for bursty and low commitment. Private brings the security but can have higher operational premium. we'll send a cost model comparing hosted/dedicated/private for your expected qps and sequence lengths.

[26:30] Diego: benchmarks — we'll propose a test plan: 1) baseline latency for 8k context across MPT-30B, 2) throughput with batching to emulate your traffic, 3) cold-start sim for KV-cache behaviors. we'll provide the csv template.

[28:10] Maya: regarding network firewall rules, can you provide the exact IPs and ports we need to open? we need to add to our change window documentation.
[28:22] Diego: yes, we'll provide a concrete list. note sometimes IPs differ a bit by deployment; for PrivateLink you only need interface endpoint security groups and the destination ports (443). for peering/TGW you'll need BGP routes or static routes depending on TGW config.

[31:00] Lena: any compliance certifications?
[31:05] Aisha: we have SOC2 Type II, ISO27001, and can share penetration test summaries. I'll attach the security-pack.pdf in follow-up.

[33:40] Samir: latency SLA, is there a guarantee?
[33:47] Aisha: for Dedicated we have SLA-backed latency and uptime targets in enterprise contracts; Hosted has standard SLAs. For Private, SLA depends on deployment model and negotiation. we'll propose targets in the SOW.

[36:15] Maya: routing policy question — can we force traffic to specific model variants based on cost/latency? e.g., route low-priority requests to a quantized cheaper variant.
[36:28] Diego: yes, our smart routing supports policy-based model routing by tags (latency-sensitive vs cost-optimized). you can set automatic fallback to quantized variants. note that quantization can slightly impact quality; we have eval tooling for that.

[39:05] Lena: what's the onboarding timeline for Private?
[39:12] Aisha: typical onboarding for Private is 4-8 weeks: network setup (1-2 weeks), provisioning and KMS integration (1 week), pilot benchmarking (1-2 weeks), and then ramp. Dedicated-only pilots can be faster if you accept our managed capacity.

[41:50] Samir: okay, summary and next steps?
[41:55] Aisha: quick recap: 1) Redwood Private supports PrivateLink or peering/TGW; we'll avoid cross-account peering if you prefer; 2) BYOK + audit logs supported; 3) region us-east-1 capacity can be provisioned, we'll validate for 70B models in trial; 4) we'll send architecture doc, security pack, pricing, and benchmark plan.

[43:30] Lena: sounds good. Maya will share CIDR and firewall constraints.
[43:38] Maya: yes i'll send that today or tomorrow and add the change window dates.

[44:00] Aisha: action items: i'll email pricing and DPA, diego will prepare benchmark spreadsheet and test plan, maya to share VPC details.

[46:20] Diego: i'll also include example CloudFormation/Terraform snippets for setting up interface endpoints and the required SG rules.

[48:05] Samir: any blockers on our side? procurement wants initial TCO and a trial scope.
[48:15] Aisha: we can provide trial Dedicated cluster for 2 weeks with agreed test plan; we'll include scope for procurement.

[50:00] Lena: ok thank you, appreciate the time.
[50:05] Aisha: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and timetables.
[50:12] Diego: thanks, bye.
